assessment: Low voltage activated T-type calcium channels (CaV3.1-CaV3.3) are important to several physiological processes, but the functions of individual isoforms are difficult to distinguish pharmacologically. This study reports a spider toxin, Pn3a, which exhibits 100-fold selectivity for inhibiting CaV3.3 over CaV3.1 and CaV3.2 isoforms. This specificity is conferred by a specific interaction site on the Cav3.3 domain II voltage sensor.
